audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer carries no cooldown numbers and no sequencing at all — seven `whys`, four `spikes`, six `wants` and three prose blocks without a single "wait for X before Y". It names exactly one Locke ability (Purgatory) across the entire layer.
audit.why: The full layer already knows the answer and the content layer never inherited it: Ashen Pursuit is a flat 10s at every rank and is his only mobility, so the ten seconds after it is spent is the whole lane. Ritual Nails is 10/9/8/7/6s, Soul Ignition 18/17/16/15/14s, Purgatory 120/100/80s. A player reading only the loading-screen content gets "keep leaning on him" with no idea when.
audit.corrected: Ashen Pursuit: flat 10s at every rank, his only exit — commit in that window. Ritual Nails: 10s at rank 1, 950 range. Soul Ignition: 18s at rank 1. Purgatory: 120s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere states when Soul Ignition's healing actually lands.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Locke ignites his soul, gaining Attack Speed and Move Speed, and dealing damage to himself. At the end of the duration, Locke will heal back a portion of the damage he takes during the effect." The refund is a single payment at expiry, not sustain during the fight. That makes Grievous Wounds timing binary rather than gradual — applied any time before the duration ends, it cuts the entire refund; applied after, it does nothing. _missing-interactions.json flags needs-antiheal for this pairing and the content layer never mentions anti-heal at all.
audit.corrected: Soul Ignition pays him back only when the duration expires. Land Grievous Wounds before that moment and the whole refund is cut; he also enters the trade having already damaged himself.

audit.whatIsWrong: content spikes[0] and `early` assert that Tahm Kench's passive and grey health "beat his poke plan from the very first wave" without qualification.
audit.why: Ritual Nails is 950 range against Tongue Lash's 900. He out-ranges your only poke tool, so at level 1 he pokes first and you answer, not the reverse. The correct level-1 read is a step-in step-out pattern, not a range war you are told you already win.
audit.corrected: Ritual Nails 950 vs Tongue Lash 900 — he holds the range edge. Step in for the Q, step back out; do not try to trade poke for poke.
sources: champ-data/_kits/locke.json — Ritual Nails range 950; champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — Tongue Lash range 900

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never mentions Locke's marks, which the full layer correctly identifies as his entire engine.
audit.why: Ritual Nails "deal damage to and mark enemies hit. Locke can consume the marks to deal bonus damage with his attacks." The mark count sitting on you is a pre-paid burst waiting for Ashen Pursuit. The full layer says to "watch your own debuff bar like a cooldown" — the content layer, which is what shows on the loading screen, says nothing.
audit.corrected: Track your own nail-mark count. Two or three marks plus an available Ashen Pursuit is his kill script already paid for.

audit.whatIsWrong: diff is "FAVOURED" at 4/10 on a 49.75% matchup, full phases give Tahm Kench all 7 of 7 stages, and the two layers disagree with each other at Level 6 and First item.
audit.why: 49.75% over 603 games is a coin-flip. Every neighbouring entry in the same table is labelled EVEN 6/10 — Shen 49.8%, Vladimir 49.8%, Galio 49.86%, Illaoi 49.93%. FAVOURED 4/10 tells a player this is a free lane when the data says it is not. Worse, the full layer's own `why` text contradicts its own side labels: phases[4] is sided Tahm Kench while its why reads "fights now end at HIS floor", and phases[5] is sided Tahm Kench while its why reads "his blink-bite now genuinely one-shots marked squishies". Meanwhile content win[4] and win[5] say Skill for the same two stages. Three different answers again.
audit.corrected: EVEN / 6/10, matching the 49.8% cohort in the same file. Level 6 and First item belong to Locke in both layers — that is what both layers' own prose already describes.
sources: packet tahmkench.json — winRate 49.75, games 603; champ-data/tahmkench.full.js — diff labels for shen/vladimir/galio/illaoi at 49.8-49.93%

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer mentions that Tongue Lash's stun and Devour compete for the same three stacks.
audit.why: An Acquired Taste: "At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion." Tongue Lash: "If the champion already has 3 stacks, they are stunned and the stacks are consumed." Against a champion whose ultimate is an execute you want to be removed from, Devour is worth far more than a stun — but a player who fires Q at three stacks loses the option silently.
audit.corrected: Hold three stacks for Devour. The Tongue Lash stun spends the same three and leaves the ultimate unavailable.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — An Acquired Taste, Tongue Lash

audit.whatIsWrong: _missing-interactions.json flags resistances-invalidated on Soul Ignition (raw armour or MR is the wrong answer), but I am not proposing an itemization edit on that basis.
audit.why: The trueDamage flag on Soul Ignition could be derived from the self-damage rather than from damage he deals to you; Riot's short text does not distinguish. Asserting "his steroid deals true damage, build HP not resists" from an ambiguous derived flag would be speculation, so I left the itemization strings alone. Flagging it so a human with the wiki can settle it.

notes: Locke's full layer is the best-written entry in this slice — it already contains the Ashen Pursuit 10s window, the mark-count-as-cooldown idea and the execute-floor discipline. The content layer inherited none of it, which is why the packet flags this matchup for zero sequencing: the loading-screen text names one ability in the whole file. Most of my content edits are transplanting facts the full layer already had right. Three enum-style edits will fail a strict +/-10% length band and need applying by hand: full diff ("FAVOURED" -> "EVEN") and full phases[4].side / phases[5].side ("Tahm Kench" -> "Locke"). The content win[4]/win[5] flips happen to be length-neutral ("Skill" and "Locke" are both 5 characters) so those should apply cleanly. I did not verify the "125 range" and "Lich Bane" claims in the full layer against anything — they are not derivable from the kit file, so I left them untouched.
